clue.text: Endless feat of Caribbean gymnastics required extension

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the dance word is cut off

parts.note: the limbo is the Caribbean dance of bending backwards under a low bar

explanation.surface: A Caribbean gymnast's routine needs to run longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of LIMBO, the West Indian dance under a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is an extension of the body, so a limb is a natural synonym here.

clue.text: Way to be brought up in life, failing inward reference

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the clue says brought up in
a failing thing breaks down, so the letters of life are rearranged
in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone's way of life is collapsing for want of introspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' gives the anagram I ELF; 'to be brought up' reverses the way. 'inward reference' describes a reflexive pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflexive pronoun refers back inward to its own subject, as in 'the thing itself'.

clue.text: On which mouse eaten by swallow, superb

indicators.note: eaten by means taken inside the swallowing word

parts.note: to swallow is to consume
a computer mouse sits on a mouse mat

explanation.surface: A mouse gets gulped down by a bird, which seems magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On which mouse' is a cryptic pointer to the MAT a computer mouse runs on; 'swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate means supremely accomplished or complete, a synonym for superb.

clue.text: 11 load of rubbish by 'omo sapiens? He plays a part

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: a dustbin holds a load of rubbish
the apostrophe shows homo has lost its first letter, an H taken off
Homo sapiens is the species man

explanation.surface: A heap of trash beside a cockney human: an actor's role, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout the puzzle '11' is read as B-less: DUSTBIN without B. The dropped aitch in ''omo' gives H OFF, and sapiens is MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustin Hoffman is an American film actor, so he is someone who plays parts.

clue.text: Bit one removed from particular measure contained in small units

indicators.note: the measure is held inside what remains of the long word
removed from says these letters are taken out of the word particular

parts.note: a bit is a part
one is I, the Roman numeral
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A small piece is removed from a particular dose, kept in little units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' leaves CULAR; 'contained' places the measure inside. 'in small units' is the definition, not part of the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellular means made up of cells, that is, organised in small separate compartments.

clue.text: 11 leader's retreat

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: Tony Blair was the British Labour leader and prime minister

explanation.surface: A party leader withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: BLAIR, the former UK prime minister, without his B.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hiding place, somewhere an animal or person retreats to.

clue.text: Important suit state sector's half ruined

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
half means taking only the first three letters of sector

explanation.surface: A public sector lies half in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes SEC from SECTOR; with STATE, 'ruined' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose outcome sets a precedent, hence an important suit.

clue.text: Boss to get a grip?

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob, and such knobs are fitted to boots and tyres to give a better grip

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small raised boss, like those on football boots that help players grip the turf.

clue.text: Found popular effect to retreat during ceasefire

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: during means the reversed piece sits inside the ceasefire word

parts.note: a truce is a ceasefire

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to effect something is to do it

explanation.surface: A popular move to pull back is set up during a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' gives OD; 'during' puts it within the ceasefire. 'Found' is the verb meaning to set up, not the past of find.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish it, as to introduce a new scheme or institution.

clue.text: 11 boy on the ball

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: Albert is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is playing football.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: ALBERT without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the ball is quick and attentive, which is what being alert means.

clue.text: They sound sad, disheartened, given son to praise

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter goes

parts.note: the blues is melancholy music, so the blues sound sad

explanation.surface: Gloomy songs, cheered by a son, earn applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle U of BLUES; then add S. This answer, read as 'B less', is the instruction behind every '11' in the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless can mean to glorify or extol, as in hymns blessing God, a synonym for praise.

clue.text: Ordered to eat tree, a lunatic swallowed

indicators.note: eating puts the scrambled letters inside the word for ordered

parts.note: told means ordered, as in told to leave

indicators.note: lunatic means crazed, so these letters go wild

explanation.surface: Someone was commanded to eat a tree, and a madman gulped it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' gives ERATE; 'to eat' places it inside. 'swallowed' means put up with, not gulped.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow an insult is to put up with it, so swallowed means tolerated.

clue.text: See 4
Somewhat doltish, I'm body-builder?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A gym-goer admits to being a bit dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'doltisH I'M BOdy'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A himbo is slang for a muscular, attractive man who is not very bright.

clue.text: Berceuse with which Louis XIV's court composer entertains sailor

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so the sailor goes inside

parts.note: Jean-Baptiste Lully was the court composer to Louis XIV
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A French court composer has a sailor round while writing a cradle song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' puts the sailor inside the composer. 'Berceuse' is the French word for a cradle song.
explanation.definitionFit: A berceuse is a gentle cradle song, the same thing as a soothing bedtime tune.

clue.text: Struck all wrong, E flat

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be put right

explanation.surface: Every note struck wrongly, and E flat at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges STRUCK ALL as LACKLUSTR; add E. 'E flat' looks like a musical key, but 'flat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flat is dull and lacking sparkle, which is the meaning of lacklustre.

clue.text: Grass up on old couple, being philistine

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: a couple means two of the letter

explanation.surface: Someone reports a pair of oldies to the police, which is uncultured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns HAY into YAH; 'couple' doubles O. 'Grass up' reads like informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a crude, uncultivated person, from Swift's brutish creatures, so a philistine.

clue.text: Coffee order sent back for alternative?

indicators.note: sent back means the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
cha is tea, the drink offered as the alternative to coffee

explanation.surface: A coffee order is returned in favour of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns OM into MO. 'Coffee order' reads as a café request, but 'order' is the British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, named after the Yemeni port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Hotel trade gets sensitive about tripe, rip-off

indicators.note: about means placed around the remains of tripe

parts.note: a caring person is sensitive to others

indicators.note: off says the letters of rip are taken off the word tripe

explanation.surface: The hotel business is touchy about bad food and overcharging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' reads as a swindle, but 'rip' is the letters removed and 'off' the removal, leaving TE; 'about' wraps CARING round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Catering is the business of supplying food and drink, the core of the hotel trade.

clue.text: 11 muzzle for hound

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: to curb is to restrain or muzzle

explanation.surface: A muzzle intended for a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: CURB without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel dog, and hound is a general word for a dog.

clue.text: 11 star's speed

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity's fast pace.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: CELEBRITY without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness, the same as speed.

clue.text: European inspection announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for inspection is heard, not seen

parts.note: a check is an inspection

explanation.surface: An inspection of Europe is made public.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a person from the Czech Republic, a European.

clue.text: Little beast's heading off to collect source of money (English) for breakfast

indicators.note: collecting means the remaining letters gather the other pieces inside
heading off removes the first letter

parts.note: a foal is a little beast, a young horse
an ATM, a cash machine, is a source of money

explanation.surface: A young animal sets off to pick up cash for its morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves OAL, and 'to collect' puts the cash machine and E inside it; 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal porridge is a traditional breakfast dish, so the word can stand for a breakfast.

clue.text: Probe one criminal over sign of fire

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lag is slang for a convict, especially an old lag
Leo is one of the three fire signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Investigate one offender with a history of arson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns I LAG round to GALI. 'Probe' looks like a verb but is a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo was the NASA space probe sent to Jupiter, named after the astronomer.

clue.text: 11 rubbish where some store it?

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: garbage is rubbish

explanation.surface: Where does one keep junk?
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: GARBAGE without the B. The question mark notes that many garages fill up with junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is a storage shed for a car, where many people pile their junk too.

clue.text: 11 country having to intimidate

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: Lebanon is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A nation is obliged to bully.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: LEBANON without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is an idiom for pressuring or threatening them.

clue.text: Woman's protecting leafy area, one offering shelter

indicators.note: protecting means the woman's word wraps round the leafy area

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
an arbour is a shady leafy bower

explanation.surface: A woman shields her garden bower, giving refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' wraps the woman round the bower; 'Woman's' reads as a possessive but just gives the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbourer is a person who harbours, giving shelter or refuge to someone.

clue.text: Run shock report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for shock is spoken out

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: Flee at news of a scare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright but means a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, as a hare does.

clue.text: 11 thin, put on ten stone

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: bony means skinny or thin
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A slim person piles on ten stone.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: BONY without the B, plus X. 'Stone' looks like a British unit of weight (14 pounds).
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: 11 sturdy old hat

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: stable means firm and sturdy

explanation.surface: A robust vintage hat.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: STABLE without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat means unoriginal and tired, which is what stale means for ideas.

clue.text: Arnie's last option melted? "I'll be back!"

indicators.note: last means the final letter of Arnie's name
when the ice melts it is gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a choice is an option

explanation.surface: Schwarzenegger's final choice has thawed as he delivers his famous catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' takes ICE out of CHOICE, leaving CHO. Arnie is Arnold Schwarzenegger, whose Terminator line is quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound that comes back to you, so it might say it will be back.

clue.text: 11 drink, hot

indicators.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, read as 'B less', telling us to drop a B

parts.note: brandy is a drink

explanation.surface: A strong drink, served warm.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is read as B-less: BRANDY without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot in the sense of sexually aroused is a synonym for randy.

clue.text: Bird gathering seed, duck — hard to find insect

indicators.note: gathering means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
a germ is a seed or embryo
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the letter O
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bird collects seed, while a duck struggles to find a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' takes in both seed and duck; the hard letter follows. 'Bird' tempts as the definition, but the answer is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger moth is a moth with boldly patterned wings, so an insect.
